chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem with the Salam (advance payment) in animals when you name a known thing.

key_terms.السَّلَمِ: Salam, a forward sale contract where payment is made in advance for goods to be delivered later.
key_terms.الْحَيَوَانِ: Animals, specifically livestock in this commercial context.
key_terms.مَعْلُوماً: Known, referring to the specific identification of the subject matter to ensure validity.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay in advance for animals in Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the Salam contract for livestock, a practice crucial for pre-Islamic and early Islamic agrarian economies, by stipulating that the subject matter must be clearly specified to eliminate gharar (ambiguity). In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith is foundational for distinguishing between permissible forward sales and those rendered invalid by excessive uncertainty regarding the delivered goods. It underscores the principle that while advance payment is allowed, the commodity's attributes must be sufficiently defined to ensure fairness and prevent dispute.
